rationale:
Evidence: the raced design with sensors at y = 0.06, kd 1.1, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction line loss scored 395.35 (iterations 8, 9 and 10 are the same design). On the oval it finished 20 of 20 runs, mean 949.7 and mean time 1.869 s. On s-bend and slalom it left the track in every run, at progress 0.395 and 0.178. The kd sweep at fixed kp and base_speed rose from 0.4 (no finishes, about 57) to 0.8 (14 of 20 oval finishes, 340) to 1.1 (20 of 20, 395), so 1.1 is the best value actually raced.

Decision: I accept the critique's central point that the draft was not the raced design, and I return the exact raced geometry and controller. I reject the critique's suggestion to test kd between 1.8 and 2.5. That value has never been run, and this is the last iteration, so no run remains to check it before the unseen-track race. An untested kd could lose the oval finish, which is the only source of the 500-point completion term. The trade-off is that a sharper unseen track may fail as s-bend and slalom did, but the raced evidence is the only basis I can defend.

I keep the observation request unchanged so the final race is measured on the same metrics as the development runs.

Expected result: about 950 per run on an oval-like track, and about 395 averaged over the three development tracks. Unseen-track performance is uncertain and is not expected to exceed the oval's curvature tolerance.
